extracted.intended_audience: community water system owners/operators and state primacy agencies responsible for preparing and distributing Consumer Confidence Reports (CCRs)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and delivering Consumer Confidence Reports (CCRs) for community water systems in compliance with EPA CFR Part 141 requirements, including required content, presentation, delivery, and recordkeeping. Covers contaminant data reporting, health/education language, special-case templates (lead, coliforms, Cryptosporidium, radon), and procedural/reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prescribed definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must use the following definitions for the terms listed below if the terms are used in the report unless the system obtains written approval from the state to use an alternate definition: (i) Pesticide: Generally, any substance or mixture of substances intended for preventing, destroying, repelling, or mitigating any pest. (ii) Herbicide: Any chemical(s) used to control undesirable vegetation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative definitions require written state approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and consumer-understandable data presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: The data relating to contaminants must be presented in the reports in a manner that is clear and understandable for consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data may be displayed in one table or several adjacent tables. Any additional monitoring results a community water system chooses to include must be displayed separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source and timeframe of data included
rubrics_metrics.description: Data must be derived from data collected to comply with EPA and State monitoring and analytical requirements during the previous calendar year, or the most recent calendar year before the previous calendar year, with specified exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a system is allowed to monitor less often than annually, include date and results of most recent sampling and a brief statement that data are from most recent testing done in accordance with regulations. No data older than 5 years need be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include MCL for each detected regulated contaminant
rubrics_metrics.description: For each detected regulated contaminant (listed in appendix A to this subpart), the contaminant data section(s) must contain: The MCL for that contaminant expressed as a number equal to or greater than 1.0 (as provided in appendix A to this subpart).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express the MCL in the same units used for reporting (see appendix A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include MCLG for each detected regulated contaminant
rubrics_metrics.description: For each detected regulated contaminant the contaminant data section(s) must contain the MCLG for that contaminant expressed in the same units as the MCL.

rubrics_metrics.name: When no MCL exists, indicate treatment technique or action level
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is no MCL for a detected contaminant, the contaminant data section(s) must indicate that there is a treatment technique, or specify the action level, applicable to that contaminant, and the report must include the definitions for treatment technique and/or action level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the definitions as specified in paragraph (c)(3) of the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highest contaminant level and range for MCL contaminants
rubrics_metrics.description: For contaminants subject to an MCL (except turbidity and E. coli), the contaminant data section(s) must contain the highest contaminant level used to determine compliance with an NPDWR and the range of detected levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When compliance is determined annually or less frequently: include highest detected level at any sampling point and the range. When compliance is determined by a running annual average: include the highest average of any monitoring location and the range of individual sample results. For TTHM and HAA5, include highest locational running annual average(s) and range(s); if multiple locations exceed the MCL include all locational RAAs that exceed the MCL. Note: when rounding to determine compliance is allowed, rounding should be done prior to multiplying by the factor in appendix A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidity reporting specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting turbidity, include the appropriate metric depending on the reporting requirement: highest average monthly value (per §141.13), highest monthly value (per §141.71), or highest single measurement and lowest monthly percentage of samples meeting turbidity limits (per §§141.73/141.173/141.551).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report should include an explanation of the reasons for measuring turbidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead and copper reporting metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: For lead and copper: the report must contain the 90th percentile concentration of the most recent round(s) of sampling, the number of sampling sites exceeding the action level, and the range of tap sampling results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include likely source(s) of detected contaminants
rubrics_metrics.description: The contaminant data section(s) must include the likely source(s) of detected contaminants to the best of the operator's knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific information from sanitary surveys and source water assessments when available. If operator lacks specific information, include one or more of the typical sources for that contaminant listed in appendix A that is most applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: E. coli reporting metric (subpart Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: For E. coli analytical results under subpart Y: the report must include the total number of E. coli positive samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate data for multiple independent distribution systems
rubrics_metrics.description: If a community water system distributes water from multiple hydraulically independent distribution systems fed by different raw water sources, the contaminant data section(s) should differentiate contaminant data for each service area and identify each separate distribution system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If displayed in a table, include a separate column for each service area; alternatively produce separate reports tailored to each service area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly identify violations in contaminant data
rubrics_metrics.description: The detected contaminant data section(s) must clearly identify any data indicating violations of MCLs, MRDLs, or treatment techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report must contain a clear and readily understandable explanation of the violation including: the length of the violation, the potential adverse health effects, and actions taken by the system to address the violation. To describe potential health effects, use the relevant language of appendix A to this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unregulated contaminant monitoring reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For detected unregulated contaminants for which monitoring is required, reports must present the average and range at which the contaminant was detected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report must include a brief explanation of the reasons for monitoring for unregulated contaminants (e.g., helps EPA determine occurrence and need for regulation). May use an alternative educational statement in the CCR if approved by the Primacy Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead action level exceedance reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems that exceeded the lead action level in §141.80(c), the detected contaminant data section must clearly identify the exceedance if any corrective action has been required by the Administrator or the State during the monitoring period covered by the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear and readily understandable explanation of the exceedance, steps consumers can take to reduce exposure to lead, and a description of any corrective actions the system has or will take to address the exceedance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cryptosporidium monitoring disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the system has performed any monitoring for Cryptosporidium which indicates that Cryptosporidium may be present in the source water or the finished water, the report must include: (i) A summary of the results of the monitoring; and (ii) An explanation of the significance of the results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radon monitoring disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If the system has performed any monitoring for radon which indicates that radon may be present in the finished water, the report must include: (i) The results of the monitoring; and (ii) An explanation of the significance of the results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting other contaminant monitoring that may indicate health concern
rubrics_metrics.description: If additional monitoring indicates the presence of other contaminants in the finished water that may indicate a health concern, EPA strongly encourages systems to report those results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine if results may indicate a health concern, check if EPA has proposed an NPDWR or issued a health advisory for that contaminant. EPA considers detects above a proposed MCL or health advisory level to indicate possible health concerns. For such contaminants, EPA recommends including the results and an explanation noting the existence of a health advisory or proposed regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report NPDWR compliance violations with explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to identifying contaminant violations, the report must note any violation during the period covered of specified NPDWR requirements and include a clear, readily understandable explanation of the violation, any potential adverse health effects, and steps the system has taken to correct the violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed requirements include: monitoring and reporting of compliance data; filtration and disinfection (if failed to install or equipment/process failure include prescribed language about disease-causing organisms and symptoms); lead and copper control requirements (include applicable appendix A language); treatment techniques for Acrylamide and Epichlorohydrin (include relevant appendix A language); recordkeeping of compliance data; special monitoring requirements (§§141.40/141.41); and violation of terms of a variance, exemption, or administrative/judicial order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variances and exemptions disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If a system is operating under the terms of a variance or an exemption, the report must contain: (1) An explanation of the reasons; (2) Date issued; (3) Brief status report on steps the system is taking to install treatment, find alternative sources, or otherwise comply with terms/schedules; (4) Notice of any opportunity for public input in review/renewal of the variance or exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include basic educational information on contaminants
rubrics_metrics.description: The report must contain a brief explanation regarding contaminants reasonably expected to be found in drinking water including bottled water. Systems may use the provided language or comparable language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the specified paragraphs defining that both tap and bottled water come from surface/groundwater, contaminants may include microbial/inorganic/pesticides/organic/radioactive, EPA and FDA regulate limits, presence doesn't necessarily mean risk, and contact info for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide contact information for additional information
rubrics_metrics.description: The report must include the telephone number of the owner, operator, or designee of the community water system as a source of additional information concerning the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a system uses a website or social media to share additional information, EPA recommends including how to access such media platforms in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited English proficiency (LEP) content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In communities with a large proportion of consumers with limited English proficiency, as determined by the Primacy Agency, the report must contain information in the appropriate language(s) regarding the importance of the report and either contain information where such consumers may obtain a translated copy of the report, or assistance in the appropriate language(s), or the report must be in the appropriate language(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination of 'large proportion' is by the Primacy Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public participation information
rubrics_metrics.description: The report must include information (e.g., time and place of regularly scheduled board meetings) about opportunities for public participation in decisions that may affect the quality of the water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional additional public education content
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems may include such additional information as they deem necessary for public education consistent with, and not detracting from, the purpose of the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groundwater significant deficiency and fecal contamination reporting (subpart S)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any ground water system that receives notice from the State of a significant deficiency or notice from a laboratory of a fecal indicator-positive ground water source sample that is not invalidated must inform its customers of any significant deficiency that is uncorrected at the time of the next reporting period or of any fecal indicator-positive ground water source sample in the next report or 6-month update. The system must continue to inform the public annually until the State determines the deficiency is corrected or contamination addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each report must include: nature of deficiency or source/date(s) of fecal-positive samples; if contamination addressed and date; for unaddressed deficiencies, the State-approved plan and schedule for correction including interim measures and progress; and if a fecal-positive source sample not invalidated, potential health effects using appendix A language.

rubrics_metrics.name: If State-directed correction prior to report, disclose correction details
rubrics_metrics.description: If directed by the State, a system with significant deficiencies corrected before the next report must inform customers of the significant deficiency, how it was corrected, and the date of correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disclosure follows the subpart S reporting elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coliform Level 1/Level 2 assessment report templates (subpart Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems required to comply with Level 1 or Level 2 assessment requirements that are not due to an E. coli MCL violation must include specified template text describing coliforms, the number of assessments conducted, corrective actions taken, and statements about failures to conduct assessments or correct identified defects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems may use an alternative statement with equivalent information for certain subparagraphs if approved by the primacy agency. Templates include text to be filled in (e.g., number of assessments, number of corrective actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: E. coli-related Level 2 assessment template and health language (subpart Y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any system required to conduct a Level 2 assessment due to an E. coli MCL violation must include specified text describing that E. coli was found and that detailed assessments and corrective actions were required, plus health effects language in appendix A and statements if required assessments or corrections were not completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems may use alternative equivalent statements for some parts if approved by primacy agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements describing specific E. coli noncompliance scenarios
rubrics_metrics.description: If a system detects E. coli and has violated the E. coli MCL, in addition to tables required, the system must include one or more specified statements describing noncompliance scenarios (e.g., E. coli-positive repeat sample following total coliform-positive routine sample; failures to take required repeat samples or test for E. coli).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If E. coli detected but not in violation, system may include a statement explaining detection without violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead tap sampling data availability notice (subpart I)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report must notify consumers that complete lead tap sampling data are available for review and must include information on how to access the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service line inventory statement and access instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The report must include a statement that a service line inventory has been prepared (including inventories showing no lead/galvanized requiring replacement/lead status unknown) and include instructions to access the publicly accessible service line inventory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inventory is online, include the direct link to the inventory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service line replacement plan access information
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems with lead/galvanized requiring replacement/or lead status unknown service lines, the report must include information on how to obtain a copy of the service line replacement plan or a direct link to the plan if the system is required to make it available online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plainly worded corrosion control explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: The report must contain a plainly worded explanation of the corrosion control efforts the system is taking in accordance with subpart I, describing treatment (e.g., pH adjustment, alkalinity adjustment, corrosion inhibitor) and other efforts (e.g., monitoring to assess corrosivity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System may use one of the provided templates for systems with or without State/EPA-designated Optimal Corrosion Control Treatment, or use their own explanation that includes equivalent information. Templates specify including treatment methods, monitoring frequency/parameters, and any ongoing studies of corrosion control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of required sampling in schools and child care facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The report must include a statement that the water system is required to sample for lead in schools and licensed child care facilities as requested by the facility and direct the public to contact their school or child care facility for information about potential sampling results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominent vulnerable populations health language (§141.154(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: All reports must prominently display the language warning that some people may be more vulnerable to contaminants (immuno-compromised, elderly, infants) and advising them to seek advice from health care providers; provide contact info for EPA/CDC guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include Safe Drinking Water Hotline number and EPA safewater website reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arsenic informational statement requirement (§141.154(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A system that detects arsenic above 0.005 mg/L and up to and including 0.010 mg/L must include a short informational statement about arsenic, with example language noting arsenic causes cancer and other effects, that the utility meets the EPA arsenic MCL, and the highest concentration found in the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May use an alternative educational statement in the CCR if approved by the Primacy Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nitrate informational statement requirement (§141.154(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A system which detects nitrate at levels above 5 mg/L but below the MCL must include a short informational statement about impacts on infants (including advice about formula and alternative water sources), note that nitrate levels above 10 ppm pose high risk for infants under 6 months, explain sampling frequency, and include the highest level found during the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May use an alternative educational statement in the CCR if approved by the Primacy Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead-specific educational content requirement (§141.154(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Every report must include lead-specific information: a short informational statement about lead in drinking water and its effects on children, containing specified content (see Figure 1) including causes of lead in water, variability of lead levels, steps to reduce exposure (use certified filters, use cold water, flush pipes, boiling doesn't remove lead), and contact info and EPA link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May use an alternative educational statement in the CCR if approved by the Primacy Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct delivery requirement of reports (§141.155(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraph (g), each community water system must directly deliver a copy of the report to each customer using at minimum one of: (i) Mail or hand deliver a paper copy; (ii) Mail a notification that the report is available on a website via a direct link; (iii) Email a direct link or electronic version of the report; or (iv) Another direct delivery method approved in writing by the primacy agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems using electronic delivery must provide a paper copy upon request and notifications must prominently display directions for requesting such copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic delivery availability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that post the report to a website and provide notification must ensure the report is publicly available on the website at the time notification is made; notifications must prominently display the link and explain the nature of the link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems may use a web page to convey the information required in §§141.153, 141.154, and 141.156.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website public access retention period
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems that use a publicly available website to provide reports must maintain public access to the report for no less than 3 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good faith effort to reach non-bill-paying consumers
rubrics_metrics.description: The system must make a good faith effort to reach consumers who do not get water bills, using means recommended by the primacy agency and tailored to the consumers served by the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include posting reports online; mailing reports or postcards with links to all service addresses/postal customers; opt-in emails/texts; advertising in news/social media; publication in local paper; posting copies or notices with QR codes in public places; delivery of multiple copies for single-biller customers; delivery to community organizations; holding public meetings. Encouraged to directly deliver to service addresses where many non-bill-paying consumers. Where many bill-paying consumers lack electronic access, use at least one non-electronic form of delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report submission and certification to primacy agency
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than 10 days after the date the system is required to distribute the report to its customers, each community water system must provide a copy of the report to the primacy agency and a certification that the report(s) has/have been distributed to customers, and that the information is correct and consistent with the compliance monitoring data previously submitted to the primacy agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver report to other agencies/clearinghouses as directed
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than the date the system is required to distribute the report to its customers, each community water system must deliver the report to any other agency or clearinghouse identified by the primacy agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide reports on request and ensure accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Each community water system must make its reports available to the public upon request and should make a reasonable effort to provide the reports in an accessible format to anyone who requests an accommodation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting requirement for large systems (50,000+)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each community water system serving 50,000 or more persons must post its current year's report to a publicly-accessible site on the internet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of mailing requirement for small systems (Governor/Tribal leader)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor of a State or their designee, or the Tribal Leader where eligible, can waive the mailing requirement for community water systems serving fewer than 10,000 persons. Such systems must publish reports in local newspapers or online news sites, inform customers that reports will not be mailed, and make reports available upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems serving 500 or fewer may forego publication if they provide notice that the report is available upon request at least once per year by mail, door-to-door delivery, or posting in locations where persons served can reasonably be expected to see it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of CCR copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Any system subject to this subpart must retain copies of its Consumer Confidence Report for no less than 3 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEP assistance plan for very large systems (100,000+)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems serving 100,000 or more persons must develop a plan for providing assistance to consumers with limited English proficiency, evaluating languages spoken and the approach to address translation needs. The first plan must be provided to the state with the first report in 2027; plans must be evaluated annually and updated as necessary and reported with the certification to the primacy agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual distribution timing and data year
rubrics_metrics.description: Each community water system must distribute reports by July 1 each year. Each report distributed by July 1 must use data collected during, or prior to, the previous calendar year using methods described in paragraph (a) of the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biannual distribution requirement for systems 10,000+
rubrics_metrics.description: Each community water system serving 10,000 or more persons must distribute the report biannually (twice per calendar year) by December 31 using methods described in paragraph (a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-month update requirements for biannual systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems required to distribute biannually that have a violation or action level exceedance between Jan 1 and June 30, or received certain monitoring results, must include a 6-month update with the second report that includes: a short description of the nature of the 6-month update; if MCL/MRDL/treatment technique violation include applicable contaminant section information and a readily understandable explanation including length, health effects (appendix A language), actions taken, and expected timeframe to complete actions; if any other violation include information per §141.153(f); if lead action level exceeded include information per §141.153(d)(4)(vi) and (d)(8); and for certain monitoring results include required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 6-month update must cover monitoring results received after July 1 that were collected during the reporting year but not included in initial report as required.
